newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Solid says to keep market leadership.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Solid says to keep market leadership.

text.p: Solid Group Inc said on Thursday it will maintain its dominance in the Philippine consumer electronics industry despite a heightened price war caused by imports liberalisation.

"Solid is confident of maintaining its market leadership...The company is prepared to withstand the pressure of a protracted price war, while maintaining reasonable profit margins," president Elena Lim said at the company's stockholders meeting.
Solid is the sole franchise holder of Sony Corp and Aiwa Co Ltd products in the Philippines. It recently announced an eight-year agreement with Sony to set up Sony Philippines Inc.
Lim said new brands have taken advantage of a liberalised regime by providing lower prices.
The low television penetration rate, estimated at 10 persons per television set, also ensures demand.

"Competition is so fierce so that everybody is on his toes. But with this new joint venture with Sony, we are looking at a horizon where Sony's marketing expertise will come into play and we can expand our products even into information technology," Lim said.
The company posted a first quarter net income of 158 million pesos, higher than the previous year's 114 million pesos.
Total sales for the first three months of the year was lower at 1.6 billion pesos from the year-ago level of 1.8 billion.

"We had shortage of stock since we introduced eight new products in the first quarter. We have already solved the problem, it was just a production kink," said Celito Macachor, general manager for business development.
He said higher interest income helped boost earnings for the year. Macachor said Solid was targeting a 178 million peso net income for the first quarter.
He added that despite the lower-than-expected profit, the company will be able to meet its full-year target of one billion peso net income on core business from sales of 10 billion pesos.
In 1997, Lim said exports are expected to grow by 40 percent and the company may export more product lines aside from television units.
Last year, exports accounted for 32 percent of the company's sales.
